name: Yunzhong “Shawn” Xiao
roleBullets: Large-scale pre-training and post-training—including SFT and reinforcement learning—for conversational and multimodal foundation models.
Synthetic-data pipelines, simulated users, test-time scaling, and evaluations on distributed infrastructure.
bio:
Hi there! I am Shawn Xiao 肖云中, a Machine Learning Researcher at Apple.

I work across the full stack of foundation model capability: pre-training to **build representations**, SFT and RL to **shape behavior**, synthetic data and evaluation to **expose failure modes**, and agents and tools to turn intelligence into **reliable action**.

Currently, I work on conversational and multimodal foundation models; previously, I built multimodal AI agents for content creation on Apple Vision Pro. I studied computer systems at Carnegie Mellon University.

**My mission is to turn foundation models from fluent predictors into reliable collaborators — systems that learn deeply, act intelligently, and interact naturally with people.**

I write about how training shapes model behavior, how agents learn to use tools, and how AI can expand human thought without replacing human judgment. I am also a reviewer for **NeurIPS** and **ACL**.

Open to research conversations around foundation model training, post-training, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Reach me by [email](mailto:shawncloudy@gmail.com), connect on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yzxiao/), or explore my work on [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=b9uTwEgAAAAJ&hl=en).
mission: From fluent predictors to reliable collaborators.
missionDetail: I study how models acquire capability, how training shapes their behavior, and how intelligent systems can interact with people naturally.

agenda.title: Train intelligence
agenda.text: Pre-training and continued pre-training for multimodal, speech, and conversational foundation models—supported by large-scale data and distributed systems.

agenda.title: Shape behavior
agenda.text: SFT, reward modeling, RL/RLVR, synthetic users, test-time scaling, and evaluations that make capability boundaries visible.

agenda.title: Build collaboration
agenda.text: Agents, tool capability memory, guardrails, and full-duplex interaction that turn model intelligence into dependable human–AI collaboration.

research.title: ToolMem: Enhancing Multimodal Agents with Learnable Tool Capability Memory
research.summary: A dynamic memory for agents to learn the strengths and weaknesses of neural tools from test time experience. ToolMem improves tool-performance prediction by 14.8% in text settings and 28.7% in multimodal settings, and improves optimal tool selection by 21 and 24 percentage points.

research.title: MMPerspective: Do MLLMs Understand Perspective?
research.summary: A 10-task benchmark with 2,711 images and 5,083 question-answer pairs for testing perspective perception, spatial reasoning, and robustness across 43 multimodal large language models.

research.title: Caption Anything in Video
research.summary: CAT-V is a training-free framework for fine-grained, object-centric video captioning. It combines segmentation, temporal analysis, and multimodal prompting to produce spatially precise and temporally coherent descriptions.
